leave-management.title: Leave Management Package
leave-management.description: Explore an open-source leave management package with policy, balance and request tables, a read-only assistant, and a manual review workflow for TulipFarm.
leave-management.introduction: The leave management package brings time-off requests, recorded balances and policy guidance into one TulipFarm workspace. Each request links to a balance record, which links to a policy. Managers can inspect the evidence behind a request before making a decision.
leave-management.audience: For HR teams and managers who need a small, editable starting point for leave review. The included records use demonstration policies and employee aliases, not real employee data.
steps: After installation, replace the demonstration policy and balances with your own reviewed records. Keep the balance date so reviewers can judge whether the figures are current.
Record the request dates, requested working days and coverage plan. Link the request to the relevant employee balance.
Start the manual review workflow to prepare a recommendation. A person checks missing information and makes the leave decision.
leave-management.limitations: This package does not calculate holiday calendars, sync payroll or approve leave automatically. Recorded allowances are illustrative, not legal or employment advice. The assistant reads records; it does not change balances or approve requests.

questions.question: Does the leave management package calculate working days?
questions.answer: No. Requested working days are recorded as an input. The package does not include a holiday calendar or payroll connection, so a person must check the dates and day count.

questions.question: Can the leave assistant approve a request?
questions.answer: No. The assistant provides read-only analysis and marks missing evidence. A person remains responsible for the decision and any record changes.

marketing-content.title: Marketing Content Package
marketing-content.description: Plan campaign briefs, content calendars and editorial reviews in TulipFarm, with a read-only assistant and a manual review workflow.
marketing-content.introduction: The marketing content package connects campaigns, content items and editorial reviews in TulipFarm. Campaign records hold the audience, goal and core message. Content items link that context to a channel, target date, brief and supporting evidence.
marketing-content.audience: For marketing teams and writers who want a shared place to plan content and collect review feedback before publishing. The package provides editable records and a review procedure, not a publishing service.
steps: After installation, define a campaign audience, goal and core message before adding content items.
Build the content calendar with target dates, briefs and evidence for claims. Link each item to its campaign.
Use the manual review workflow to prepare recommendations, then record editorial feedback and decisions. A person publishes through the chosen channel.
marketing-content.limitations: There are no connected publishing channels, automatic posts or scheduled publishing jobs. The assistant cannot send messages or edit records. A person must verify claims, approve content and publish it.

questions.question: Can this package publish blog posts or social content?
questions.answer: No. It organizes campaign briefs, content items and editorial reviews. Publishing happens outside this package after a person reviews the content.

questions.question: Where does the evidence for marketing claims go?
questions.answer: Each content item includes a Claim evidence field. The review procedure can use recorded evidence and flag gaps, but a person must verify the sources before publishing.

sales-crm.title: Sales CRM Package
sales-crm.description: Explore an open-source sales CRM package with accounts, opportunities and activity records, plus a read-only deal assistant and a manual review workflow.
sales-crm.introduction: The sales CRM package organizes accounts, opportunities and sales activities in TulipFarm. Opportunities link to accounts and carry a stage, value, currency, target close date and next step. Activity records keep the notes behind a deal review in the same system.
sales-crm.audience: For founders and small sales teams who need a clear record of customer needs, deal stages and follow-up work. It is a starting point for a sales process, not a full CRM replacement.
steps: After installation, add account records with customer needs, segments and contact roles.
Link opportunities to accounts and record the current stage, value and next step. Add dated activity notes as the conversation develops.
Start the manual review workflow to examine deal evidence and missing next steps. A person decides what to do and contacts the customer.
sales-crm.limitations: The package has no email sync, automatic outreach or automated forecasting. Deal values and stages come from recorded data. The assistant cannot modify opportunities or send follow-up messages.

questions.question: Does the sales CRM package connect to email?
questions.answer: No. Accounts, opportunities and activity notes are stored in the package tables. Email sync and automatic follow-up sending are not included.

questions.question: Can I track deals in different currencies?
questions.answer: An opportunity has separate Value and Currency fields. The package does not include exchange-rate conversion or consolidated revenue forecasting.

support-desk.title: Support Desk Package
support-desk.description: Explore an open-source support desk package with queues, tickets and notes, plus a read-only assistant for reply review. A Zendesk-style starting point.
support-desk.introduction: The support desk package brings support queues, tickets and ticket notes into TulipFarm. Each queue can carry scope and escalation guidance. Tickets record the problem, priority, status and next step so reviewers can see what still needs attention.
support-desk.audience: For support teams exploring a small, editable ticket-review system. Its Zendesk-style organization is a reference to the workflow, not an affiliation, integration or full replacement.
steps: After installation, define support queues and their escalation guidance.
Add tickets with a requester alias, problem description, priority and next step. Link notes to the relevant ticket.
Use the manual review workflow to prepare triage or reply recommendations. A person checks the response and sends it through the appropriate channel.
support-desk.limitations: There is no inbox sync, SLA clock, customer portal or automatic sending. A note visibility label is stored data, not a customer-facing access-control system. The assistant cannot change tickets or contact customers.

questions.question: Is this a Zendesk integration or replacement?
questions.answer: No. This is an independent Zendesk-style starting point for organizing queues, tickets and notes in TulipFarm. It does not import from or sync with Zendesk.

questions.question: Does the support assistant send customer replies?
questions.answer: No. It prepares read-only recommendations for human review. A person must approve and send any reply through a separate support channel.

project-tracking.title: Project Tracking Package
project-tracking.description: Track projects, sprints and issues in TulipFarm with a read-only review assistant. An open-source, Jira-style starting point for project tracking.
project-tracking.introduction: The project tracking package connects projects, sprints and issues in TulipFarm. A project defines the goal, a sprint defines its time window and scope, and an issue records the work, acceptance criteria and blockers. The relationships keep delivery reviews tied to the work being discussed.
project-tracking.audience: For engineering teams that want an editable starting point for sprint and issue review. Jira-style describes the organization of the work, not an integration or feature-for-feature replacement.
steps: After installation, define a project goal and the owner role responsible for it.
Create sprints with dates and goals, then link issues with status, priority, estimates and acceptance criteria.
Start the manual review workflow to examine scope and blockers. A person decides on priorities and updates the work records.
project-tracking.limitations: The package does not provide a live board, repository integration or Jira sync. Estimates are recorded inputs, not delivery forecasts. The assistant cannot edit issues, commit code or make delivery decisions.

questions.question: Does the project tracking package sync with Jira or GitHub?
questions.answer: No. The package includes project, sprint and issue records plus a review workflow. It does not include Jira sync or a repository integration.

questions.question: What does the sprint review assistant do?
questions.answer: It reads the recorded work, follows the attached procedure, cites evidence and identifies missing information. Its recommendations need human review; it cannot change issues or approve decisions.

product-backlog.title: Product Backlog Package
product-backlog.description: Connect initiatives, work items and customer feedback in one product backlog in TulipFarm, with read-only prioritization review. Open-source.
product-backlog.introduction: The product backlog package links initiatives, backlog items and customer feedback in TulipFarm. Initiatives describe the desired outcome. Backlog items record the problem, priority, effort estimate and success signal, while feedback records preserve the observed need and limits of the evidence.
product-backlog.audience: For product teams who want to discuss priorities with customer evidence close to the work. Its Linear-style structure is an independent starting point, not a connected Linear workspace.
steps: After installation, define an initiative and the customer outcome it should support.
Link backlog items to initiatives, then attach feedback with a source description and evidence limits.
Use the manual review workflow to compare recorded needs and priorities. A person makes the prioritization decision and any roadmap commitment.
product-backlog.limitations: There is no Linear sync or automatic roadmap commitment. The package does not verify customer feedback independently. The read-only assistant suggests actions but cannot reprioritize work or modify records.

questions.question: Is this package connected to Linear?
questions.answer: No. Linear-style describes the backlog workflow. This independent package stores initiatives, backlog items and feedback in TulipFarm without syncing to Linear.

questions.question: Does the assistant decide product priorities?
questions.answer: No. It prepares evidence-based recommendations from the recorded information and marks unknowns. A person decides priorities and makes any roadmap commitments.

sprint-issue-tracker.title: Sprint and Issue Tracker
sprint-issue-tracker.outcome: Triage, plan and ship engineering work with a full history.
sprint-issue-tracker.description: Triage, plan and ship engineering work in TulipFarm: issue tracking with projects, epics, sprints and releases, plus status history automations.
sprint-issue-tracker.introduction: Sprint and Issue Tracker gives an engineering team the records it needs to plan and ship work: projects, components, epics, sprints, releases and issues, with an activity log for every status change. New issues start in triage, open issues are marked overdue the morning after their due date, and blocked issues log a blocker and ask a person to unblock them.
sprint-issue-tracker.audience: For engineering teams that want their issue tracker inside the same workspace as their other records. It follows the shape of Jira and Linear projects, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, replace the example project, components and sprint with your own, and set the team timezone used by date automations.
Create issues with a type, priority, assignee and due date, and link them to an epic, sprint and release. Issues created without a status start in triage.
Move issues through their statuses. Each change is logged in Issue activity, and blocked issues ask a person to unblock them.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant about sprint risk, blockers or release readiness.
sprint-issue-tracker.limitations: There is no Git or pull request sync, no drag-and-drop board and no velocity report. Automations only change rows in the package’s own tables. The assistant reads records and cannot edit issues or approve releases.

questions.question: Can this package replace Jira or Linear?
questions.answer: For teams that track issues, sprints and releases as records, it can. It does not sync with Jira, Linear or a code host, so commits and pull requests stay in those tools.

questions.question: Does the assistant change issue priorities?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. A person decides priorities and makes any record changes.

sla-ticket-desk.title: SLA Ticket Desk
sla-ticket-desk.outcome: Answer customers on time with SLAs, escalations and ratings.
sla-ticket-desk.description: Run customer support in TulipFarm: tickets, SLA policies, canned responses and help articles, with SLA breach and escalation automations.
sla-ticket-desk.introduction: SLA Ticket Desk holds a support team’s tickets with the organizations and customers behind them, SLA policies, ticket conversations, canned responses, help articles and satisfaction ratings. New tickets get Normal priority, status changes are logged, unsolved tickets are marked SLA breached the morning after their resolution due date, urgent tickets are escalated to the support lead, and solved tickets open a satisfaction rating.
sla-ticket-desk.audience: For support teams that want tickets and customer context in one editable workspace. It follows the shape of Zendesk and Freshdesk, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, replace the example organizations, customers and SLA policies with your own targets.
Record each ticket with its customer, channel and resolution due date. Tickets created without a priority get Normal priority.
Work the ticket through its statuses. Urgent tickets ask the support lead to take ownership, and solved tickets open a satisfaction rating for a person to send.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant about SLA risk, backlog or reply quality.
sla-ticket-desk.limitations: There is no email inbox, chat widget, customer portal or automatic sending. The resolution due date is a recorded deadline, not a business-hours clock. The assistant cannot reply to customers or change tickets.

questions.question: Does SLA Ticket Desk receive email?
questions.answer: No. Tickets are records you create in TulipFarm. Inbox and chat channels stay in your existing tools, and replies are sent outside the package.

questions.question: Can the assistant answer customers?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. A support agent decides the reply and makes any record changes.

it-incident-desk.title: IT Incident and Change Desk
it-incident-desk.outcome: Run incidents, problems and changes with approvals built in.
it-incident-desk.description: Run IT incidents, problems and changes in TulipFarm, with service requests, configuration items and change approval automations built in.
it-incident-desk.introduction: IT Incident and Change Desk records IT services and configuration items with the incidents, problems, change requests and service requests that affect them, plus an incident timeline and an on-call rota. New incidents get P3 priority, status changes are logged on the timeline, P1 incidents are marked major and the incident manager is asked to confirm command, change approval goes to a person, and unfulfilled requests are marked overdue after their due date.
it-incident-desk.audience: For IT and platform teams that want ITIL-style records without a heavyweight service platform. It follows the shape of ServiceNow and Jira Service Management, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, list your IT services and configuration items, and fill in the on-call rota.
Record incidents against a configuration item. Incidents without a priority get P3, and raising one to P1 declares a major incident.
Tick Request approval on a change request to route it to an approver, who marks it approved.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant about incident impact, related problems or next steps.
it-incident-desk.limitations: There is no monitoring integration, paging, discovery or CMDB sync. On-call entries are records, not a paging schedule. The assistant cannot approve changes or update incidents.

questions.question: Does the package page the on-call engineer?
questions.answer: No. The on-call rota is a record of who is on call. Paging and alert routing stay in your incident tooling.

questions.question: Can the assistant approve a change?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. An approver decides the change and makes any record changes.

team-wiki.title: Reviewed Team Wiki
team-wiki.outcome: Keep team docs owned, reviewed and current.
team-wiki.description: An open-source team wiki for TulipFarm with spaces, pages, review cycles and a question log, plus draft, page review and stale-page automations.
team-wiki.introduction: Reviewed Team Wiki organizes team documentation as spaces and pages, each with an owner and a review date. Page reviews record approvals and requested changes, and the question log captures what people asked but could not find. New pages start as drafts, pages moved to In review ask a reviewer to approve them, and published pages past their review date are marked stale.
team-wiki.audience: For teams that want documentation ownership and freshness tracked alongside their other work. It follows the shape of Confluence and Notion wikis, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, create a space for each team and replace the example pages with your own.
Give every page an owner and a review-by date. Pages created without a status start as drafts.
Move a page to In review to ask a reviewer to approve it. Published pages past their review date are marked stale the next morning.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant which pages are stale or which questions need a page.
team-wiki.limitations: Page bodies are plain long text; there is no rich-text editor, page tree, inline comments or version history. The assistant reads pages but cannot publish or edit them.

questions.question: Can I write formatted pages in the wiki?
questions.answer: Page content is stored as plain text in a long-text field. Use the wiki for ownership, review dates and short guidance, and keep long formatted documents in a document editor.

questions.question: Does the assistant rewrite stale pages?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. The page owner decides what to update and makes any record changes.

client-retainers.title: Client Retainers and Billing
client-retainers.outcome: Deliver client work and bill every hour.
client-retainers.description: Deliver client work and bill every hour in TulipFarm, with clients, retainers, timesheets and invoices, plus overdue invoice and renewal automations.
client-retainers.introduction: Client Retainers and Billing connects an agency’s clients, client projects and retainers with timesheets, invoices, team capacity and project updates. New time entries are marked unbilled, sent invoices are marked overdue the morning after they fall due, active retainers are marked renewal due 30 days before they renew, and at-risk projects ask the account lead to agree a recovery plan.
client-retainers.audience: For agencies and consultancies that want delivery, time and billing in one editable place. It follows the shape of Productive, Scoro and Teamwork, but it is an independent package, not an integration with those products.
steps: After installation, replace the example clients, projects and retainers with your own.
Log time against client projects. Entries without a billing status are marked unbilled so they are picked up at invoice time.
Record invoices with due dates and keep project health current. Marking a project at risk logs an update and asks the account lead for a recovery plan.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant about budget burn, unbilled time or overdue invoices.
client-retainers.limitations: There is no timer, payment processing or accounting sync. Invoices are records, not issued documents. The assistant cannot change budgets, send invoices or contact clients.

questions.question: Does the package send invoices to clients?
questions.answer: No. Invoices are records for tracking amounts and due dates. Issue and collect them through your accounting tool.

questions.question: Can the assistant approve a budget change?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. An account lead decides the budget and makes any record changes.

portfolio-planner.title: Portfolio Planner
portfolio-planner.outcome: Plan projects and catch slipping work early.
portfolio-planner.description: Plan project portfolios in TulipFarm and catch slipping work early, with tasks, milestones, status reports and overdue task automations.
portfolio-planner.introduction: Portfolio Planner organizes cross-team work into portfolios, projects, milestones and tasks, with workload plans and status reports. New tasks start as not started, unfinished tasks and upcoming milestones are flagged the morning after their date, and off-track projects open a status report and ask the owner for a recovery plan.
portfolio-planner.audience: For operations, marketing and project teams that plan work outside an engineering tracker. It follows the shape of Asana, monday.com and ClickUp, but it is an independent package, not an integration with those products.
steps: After installation, set up a portfolio and replace the example projects and milestones with your own.
Add tasks with an owner, due date and project. Tasks created without a status start as not started.
Keep project status current. Off-track projects open a status report and ask the owner for a recovery plan.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant which projects are at risk and why.
portfolio-planner.limitations: There is no Gantt chart, time tracking or dependency scheduling. Workload plans are recorded estimates, not capacity calculations. The assistant cannot reassign or reschedule work.

questions.question: Does the package reschedule tasks when a milestone slips?
questions.answer: No. It flags missed milestones and overdue tasks so a person can decide what moves. Dates only change when someone edits them.

questions.question: Can the assistant reassign tasks?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. The project owner decides who does the work and makes any record changes.

deal-pipeline.title: Deal Pipeline and Renewals
deal-pipeline.outcome: Move deals forward and never lose a renewal.
deal-pipeline.description: Move deals forward in an open-source TulipFarm CRM with companies, contacts, quotes and renewals, plus won-deal renewal and quote expiry automations.
deal-pipeline.introduction: Deal Pipeline and Renewals holds a sales team’s companies and contacts with the deals, activities, quotes and renewals that come from them. New deals start in qualification, every stage change is logged as an activity, won deals open a renewal for the account owner to date and price, and sent quotes are marked expired the morning after their expiry date.
deal-pipeline.audience: For small sales teams that want their pipeline next to the rest of the business. It follows the shape of HubSpot CRM and Pipedrive, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, replace the example companies and contacts with your own accounts.
Create deals with an amount, owner and expected close date. Deals created without a stage start in qualification.
Move deals through their stages. Each change is logged, and won deals open a renewal record.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant which deals are stalled and where to focus.
deal-pipeline.limitations: There is no email sync, sequences, calling or forecasting model. Activities are logged records, not captured emails. The assistant cannot change deals or contact customers.

questions.question: Does Deal Pipeline and Renewals sync my email?
questions.answer: No. Log important calls, meetings and emails as deal activities. Email sync and sequences stay in your existing tools.

questions.question: Does the assistant forecast revenue?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. A sales lead decides the forecast and makes any record changes.

hiring-pipeline.title: Hiring Pipeline
hiring-pipeline.outcome: Hire with structured interviews and approved offers.
hiring-pipeline.description: Hire with structured interviews in TulipFarm: job openings, candidates, scorecards and offers, plus late scorecard and offer approval automations.
hiring-pipeline.introduction: Hiring Pipeline tracks hiring from job opening to offer: candidates, applications, interviews, scorecards and offers. New applications start as applied, interviews without a submitted scorecard are marked late the next morning, applications that reach the offer stage open a draft offer, and offers sent for approval go to an approver who marks them approved.
hiring-pipeline.audience: For hiring managers and small recruiting teams that want a structured pipeline without a dedicated applicant tracking system. It follows the shape of Greenhouse and Lever, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, replace the example job opening and candidate with your own roles.
Add candidates and link each application to a job opening. Applications created without a stage start as applied.
Schedule interviews and record scorecards. Moving an application to the offer stage opens a draft offer.
Tick Request approval on an offer to route it to an approver, then start the review workflow to ask about pipeline health.
hiring-pipeline.limitations: There is no careers page, job board posting, résumé parsing or e-signature. The assistant reads candidate records for analysis but cannot make hiring decisions or contact candidates.

questions.question: Does Hiring Pipeline post jobs to job boards?
questions.answer: No. Job openings are internal records. Post roles and receive applications through your careers site or job boards, then record them here.

questions.question: Does the assistant decide who to hire?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. The hiring team decides who moves forward and makes any record changes.

product-roadmap.title: Product Roadmap
product-roadmap.outcome: Turn customer evidence into a roadmap you can defend.
product-roadmap.description: Turn customer insights into a product roadmap you can defend in TulipFarm, with features, objectives, releases and sign-off automations.
product-roadmap.introduction: Product Roadmap links customer insights to the features they support, features to objectives, and features to roadmap releases, with an update log for each feature. New insights are marked for triage, feature status changes are logged, features moved to planned ask the product lead to confirm them, and unreleased releases are marked late the morning after their target date.
product-roadmap.audience: For product managers who want discovery and roadmap decisions backed by recorded evidence. It follows the shape of Productboard and Aha!, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, set your product objectives and replace the example releases with your own.
Record customer insights with their source, then link each to the feature it supports. New insights are marked for triage.
Move features through their statuses. Every change is logged, and planned features ask the product lead to confirm them.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant what to prioritize and what evidence supports it.
product-roadmap.limitations: There is no public roadmap portal, customer voting or feedback widget. Insights are recorded by people, not captured automatically. The assistant cannot change priorities or commit to dates.

questions.question: Does the package collect customer feedback automatically?
questions.answer: No. Add insights from interviews, support tickets or sales calls as records, with a source, so the evidence stays traceable.

questions.question: Does the assistant set the roadmap?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. The product team decides the roadmap and makes any record changes.

account-health.title: Account Health and Renewals
account-health.outcome: Spot account risk early and renew with confidence.
account-health.description: Spot account risk early and renew with confidence in TulipFarm, with health checks, success plays and renewals, plus red health automations.
account-health.introduction: Account Health and Renewals tracks each customer account with its health checks, success plays, business reviews, subscription renewals and risks. New accounts are marked not scored, accounts that turn red open a risk and ask the CSM to start a recovery play, renewals move into their window 90 days ahead, and planned business reviews are marked overdue after their date.
account-health.audience: For customer success managers who want account health and renewals in one editable workspace. It follows the shape of Gainsight and Vitally, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, replace the example accounts with your customers and set an owner for each.
Record health checks and keep each account’s health current. Turning an account red opens a risk for the CSM.
Record renewal dates and business reviews. Renewals move into their window 90 days before the renewal date.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant which accounts need attention before renewal.
account-health.limitations: There is no product usage ingestion or automatic health scoring from telemetry. Health is a recorded judgement. The assistant cannot change health, contact customers or adjust renewals.

questions.question: Does the package calculate health from product usage?
questions.answer: No. Health is set by people from health checks and other evidence. Usage data stays in your analytics tools.

questions.question: Can the assistant contact at-risk customers?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. The account owner decides the outreach and makes any record changes.

employee-lifecycle.title: Employee Lifecycle
employee-lifecycle.outcome: Keep people records, onboarding and reviews on track.
employee-lifecycle.description: Keep employee records, onboarding and performance reviews on track in TulipFarm, an open-source HRIS package with offboarding and expiry automations.
employee-lifecycle.introduction: Employee Lifecycle keeps core people records: employees, job roles, onboarding and offboarding tasks, performance reviews and employee documents. New employees get an onboarding task, employees marked leaving get an offboarding task and their manager is asked to confirm handover, incomplete reviews are marked overdue after their due date, and documents are marked expiring soon 30 days before they expire.
employee-lifecycle.audience: For small companies that need an employee record and lifecycle tasks before buying a full HR platform. It follows the shape of BambooHR and HiBob, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, set up job roles and replace the example employees with your team.
Add new hires. Each new employee gets an onboarding task for their manager to plan.
Record performance review due dates and document expiry dates so both are flagged in time.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant about overdue reviews or expiring documents.
employee-lifecycle.limitations: There is no payroll, benefits, time-off accrual or e-signature. Records hold personal data, so limit access to the people team. The assistant reads records but cannot change employment details.

questions.question: Does Employee Lifecycle run payroll?
questions.answer: No. It stores employee records and lifecycle tasks. Payroll and benefits stay in your payroll provider.

questions.question: Can the assistant change employee records?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. The people team decides any change and makes any record changes.

compliance-controls.title: Compliance Controls and Evidence
compliance-controls.outcome: Keep controls, evidence and risks audit-ready.
compliance-controls.description: Keep compliance controls, evidence and risks audit-ready in TulipFarm, with policies, vendors and audits, plus failing-control and expiry automations.
compliance-controls.introduction: Compliance Controls and Evidence tracks security policies, controls, control evidence, compliance risks, third-party vendors and audits. New vendors are marked unassessed, failing controls open a risk and ask the control owner for a treatment plan, evidence is marked expired the morning after it expires, and approved policies past their review date are marked review overdue.
compliance-controls.audience: For security and compliance leads preparing for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 who want controls and evidence tracked as records. It follows the shape of evidence tracking in Vanta and Drata, but it is an independent package, not an integration with either product.
steps: After installation, replace the example policies and controls with your framework’s controls and owners.
Record evidence for each control with an expiry date, and keep control status current.
Add vendors as you onboard them. A failing control opens a compliance risk for its owner to treat.
Start the review workflow to ask the read-only assistant about audit readiness and gaps.
compliance-controls.limitations: There is no automated evidence collection, cloud scanning or auditor portal. The package does not certify compliance. The assistant cannot accept risks or mark controls as passing.

questions.question: Does Compliance Controls and Evidence collect evidence automatically?
questions.answer: No. Evidence is recorded by control owners with a link or description and an expiry date. Automated collection stays in your security tooling.

questions.question: Can the assistant accept a risk?
questions.answer: No. It reads the package tables, cites the rows behind each finding and marks unknowns. The risk owner decides whether to accept it and makes any record changes.

client-onboarding.title: Client Onboarding Checklist
client-onboarding.outcome: Kick off every new client the same way, with nothing missed.
client-onboarding.description: Kick off every new client the same way in TulipFarm, with client onboarding checklists and access requests, plus automations that flag late work.
client-onboarding.introduction: Client Onboarding Checklist gives an agency one record per new client, a checklist of setup tasks and a log of the access, assets and contacts it still needs. New onboardings open a kickoff task and an access task, unfinished tasks are marked late the morning after their due date, and blocked access requests ask the account lead to follow up.
client-onboarding.audience: For agencies and client-service teams that onboard several clients a month and want the same kickoff every time, instead of a copied spreadsheet per client.
steps: After installation, replace the example client with a real onboarding and set the team timezone used by the late-task automation.
Create an onboarding for each new client. The kickoff and access tasks are added for you; add any others your service needs.
Log each access or asset request and move it to received or blocked. Blocked requests ask the account lead to follow up.
